summary: Enterprise AI model API aggregators have become the dominant way corporations consume foundation models in 2026, offering secure, managed access to models like GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini, and Mistral without data leaving the customer's trusted cloud boundary. The market is led by the three hyperscalers (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, Google Vertex AI), with data-platform-native entrants like Snowflake Cortex and Databricks, plus IBM watsonx, Oracle, and edge-focused Cloudflare Workers AI serving specialized niches. There is no single winner — selection is driven primarily by existing cloud contracts, data gravity, compliance posture, and which specific models an organization needs.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay within the customer's own cloud tenant/VPC and are not used to train vendor models, satisfying strict governance requirements.

Consolidated compliance and security: aggregators inherit the cloud's certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, ISO, GDPR) plus native IAM, encryption, and private networking, avoiding separate vendor security reviews.
Single billing and existing contracts: AI spend flows through committed cloud spend/EDP agreements and one invoice rather than negotiating and paying each model vendor directly.
Model flexibility and avoiding lock-in: a single API gives access to many competing models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, Cohere, Gemini, GPT) so teams can switch or route without re-architecting.

Unified enterprise tooling: centralized audit logging, observability, guardrails, access controls, and integration with data already sitting in the same cloud reduce operational and data-movement overhead.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
available_models: models via Azure AI Foundry model catalog
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M input and output tokens, plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved, predictable capacity; image and audio priced per unit.
key_features: Content filtering and Azure AI Content Safety guardrails
Audit logs via Azure Monitor and Microsoft Purview
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure that want first-class, early access to OpenAI frontier models with strong compliance and Microsoft 365/Copilot integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing per model, plus Provisioned Throughput (hourly commitment for reserved capacity); batch inference offered at discount.
key_features: Bedrock Guardrails for safety and PII redaction
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the widest multi-vendor model choice (especially Anthropic Claude) with deep native AWS security and agent tooling.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (per 1M characters/tokens) on-demand, plus Generative AI Scale Units (GSUs) for provisioned throughput — e.g., ~25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields roughly 67,250 tokens/second sustained.
key_features: VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect
Audit logging via Cloud Audit Logs
Vertex AI Agent Builder and RAG Engine
Safety filters and Responsible AI tooling
platforms.best_for: Data- and analytics-heavy enterprises on Google Cloud wanting Gemini plus a broad model garden with strong BigQuery/data integration and regional controls.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumed as Snowflake credits based on tokens processed; serverless functions metered per token, billed through existing Snowflake account.
key_features: Runs inside the Snowflake governance boundary (data never leaves)
SQL and Python (Cortex functions) access to LLMs
Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search (RAG over governed data)
Row/column-level access controls apply to AI
platforms.best_for: Organizations with their data warehouse in Snowflake that want to run LLMs directly against governed data without ETL or moving data out.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI (Foundation Model APIs)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token for Foundation Model APIs and provisioned throughput options, billed via Databricks (DBU) consumption on the underlying cloud.
key_features: Unity Catalog governance over models and data
Mosaic AI Gateway for routing and rate limiting
AI/BI, Agent Framework, and vector search
platforms.best_for: Data engineering/ML-mature enterprises using the lakehouse that want to combine custom model training, RAG, and foundation model APIs under unified governance.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) token-based pricing with SaaS and on-prem/hybrid (Cloud Pak) licensing; predictable subscription options.
key_features: Hybrid and on-prem deployment (Cloud Pak for Data)
watsonx.governance for model lifecycle, risk, and audit
watsonx Orchestrate for multi-platform AI agents
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises and governments needing hybrid/on-prem deployment, IP indemnification, and strong AI governance/compliance tooling.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character/per-token on-demand pricing plus dedicated AI cluster (hosting) units for reserved capacity, billed via OCI.
key_features: Audit via OCI logging and IAM
Tight integration with Oracle Database / Fusion apps
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion customers, and sovereignty-focused public sector buyers wanting isolated dedicated capacity.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: models routed via AI Gateway (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use billed as Neurons (compute units) per inference; generous free tier and usage-based scaling, no capacity reservation needed.
key_features: Serverless inference at the network edge (low latency, global)
AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and multi-provider routing
Tight fit with Workers edge apps
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises building low-latency, globally distributed edge AI applications who want lightweight open models and provider-agnostic gateway routing.

platforms.name: NVIDIA NIM / AI Enterprise
available_models: wide catalog of optimized open models (NIM microservices)
platforms.pricing: Licensed per GPU via NVIDIA AI Enterprise subscription; self-hosted inference means cost is infrastructure + license rather than per-token.
key_features: Deploy anywhere: on-prem, any cloud, air-gapped
Full data control in customer environment
platforms.best_for: Enterprises needing maximum data control, on-prem/air-gapped deployment, or GPU-level performance optimization for self-hosted open models.
